title: Mutton 101: How To Choose The Perfect Cut For Curry, Biryani And Kebabs
text: The taste and quality of mutton depend on the cut you choose. Experts recommend deciding what dish you want to cook before buying. Instead of just saying “give me mutton”, ask for specific parts — like leg, shoulder, ribs, or loin — since each has a unique flavour, texture, and price. Planning a rich mutton curry, spicy gravy, or hearty soup? Leg, thigh, or shoulder cuts are ideal. These parts have a perfect balance of meat and fat, giving your curry a thick, flavourful gravy. Ask for a “leg and shoulder mix” at the shop — it cooks beautifully in a handi or pressure cooker. For mutton fry or sukka, the chest (breast ribs) and shoulder are your best bets. With their higher fat content, the meat stays juicy and flavourful — even after frying. No dry bites here! Making pulao or biryani? Large leg (raan) and loin cuts are perfect. Tender and sturdy, these pieces hold their shape while cooking, making your dish look as good as it tastes. At the shop, request “large leg pieces for biryani”. For a nourishing soup or light broth, pick mutton with bones — like neck or leg pieces. The bones release rich flavour and nutrients, making your soup both delicious and healthy. For kebabs, tikka, or grilled delights, choose tender cuts from the loin or inner leg. These meaty, bone-light pieces cook quickly and are perfect for juicy, flavourful grilling. Cooking for kids or someone recovering from illness? Go for soft leg or waist meat — it’s gentle on the stomach and easy to digest. Picking the right mutton cut for your dish makes every meal more delicious and satisfying.
